source_map.note: support.apple.com Tech Specs page per Mac, Chip section: 'Apple M3 chip'. Page ids: 111883 (MBA M1), 111867 (MBA M2), 111902 (M1 Pro/Max), 111900 (Mac Studio 2022), 111340 (M2 Pro/Max), 111835 (Mac Studio 2023), 117735/117736 (M3, M3 Pro/Max), 121552/121553 (M4, M4 Pro/Max), 121555 (Mac mini 2024), 122211 (Mac Studio 2025), 125405/126318 (M5, M5 Pro/Max), 128107 (Mac Studio M5 Max/M5 Ultra), 128108 (Mac mini M6/M5 Pro).

Apple newsroom press release: the page text reads 'PRESS RELEASE <Month D, YYYY>' before the headline, and the URL path holds /YYYY/MM/. Read per chip: s1, s2, s23, s24, s25, s26, s3, s27, s4, s28, s16, s17, s18.

Tech Specs Chip section: 'N-core CPU with X performance cores and Y efficiency cores' (M5 and later: 'super cores' and 'performance cores'). Soft hyphens (U+00AD) or U+2010 hyphens occur in some pages (s11, s14, s21, s22); a quote must carry them as the page does. Where a configure-to-order chip variant has no split on the support page the newsroom gives it (s3, s27, s28).
Same Chip section; the larger GPU variant is in the 'Configurable to' line (M1 Ultra 64-core on s12, M2 Ultra 76-core on s13, M2 Max 38-core on s7).
Tech Specs Memory section: base size and 'Configurable to' list with the chip variant in brackets. The brackets decide which row an option belongs to.

Tech Specs Chip section: '100GB/s memory bandwidth'; for chips with a configurable bigger variant the 'Configurable to' line carries '(546GB/s memory bandwidth)'. Ultra chips of the M5 generation say '1.2TB/s'. NOT stated for M1 on any Apple page read (s1, s11); newsroom s18 says M6 is '2.5x' M1 but gives no M1 number. M6 16GB: apple.com/mac-mini/specs (s34), column-aligned.
searched: newsroom pages, support.apple.com Tech Specs, apple.com/mac-mini/specs by search; Apple says only 'unified memory'. No LPDDR name on an Apple page.
developer.apple.com 'Determining Instruction Set Characteristics' (s33) is script-only: page.py reads 294 characters. A web search found no Apple page that ties SME, I8MM, BF16 or DotProd to a chip.
M5 generation onward: the Tech Specs Chip section lists 'Neural Accelerators' right after the GPU core count (s19, s20, s21, s22). M1 to M4: no Apple page read names GPU matrix units.

WWDC20 session 10632 (Apple silicon GPU): 'The operator core contains both a 16-bit and a 32-bit ALU'. A statement about the Apple silicon GPU in general, not a per-chip table. The per-chip Metal Feature Set Tables are a PDF (s32), not readable here.

WWDC25 session 205: 'Metal 4 is compatible with M1 (and later) and A14 Bionic (and later) Apple chips.' The per-chip GPU family table is the PDF s32 (blocked) and developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlgpufamily/apple9 (script-only, 270 characters).

cores.quote: 8-core CPU with 4 perform­ance cores and 4 efficiency cores
cores.note: the page spells 'perform<soft hyphen>ance'; page's tier names: 'performance cores' and 'efficiency cores' (newsroom pages call them high-performance and high-efficiency); key 'efficient' = efficiency cores

gpu_cores.quote: 7-core GPU, 8-core GPU

type.why: Apple pages say only 'unified memory'; no page of Apple's read names the DRAM type

sizes_gb.quote: 8GB unified memory Configurable to 16GB

bandwidth_gbps.why: Apple states no number for M1: searched M1 newsroom page (s1: no GB/s), MacBook Air M1 specs (s11), Mac mini M1 (support 111894) and MacBook Pro 13 M1 (support 111897) pages, all without a bandwidth line; later newsroom pages give only ratios ('50 percent more than M1' on s24, 'nearly 6x that of M1' on s2). Archived 2020 apple.com spec pages: web.archive.org answered 429 (blocked). No derivation from a ratio.

isa.why: Apple's sysctl instruction-set page is script-only; no Apple page read ties instruction set extensions to this chip

matrix.name.why: no Apple page read documents GPU matrix units for this chip; 'Neural Accelerators' appear from M5 on

fp16.quote: The operator core contains both a 16-bit and a 32-bit ALU so it can perform math at different precisions to reduce power usage and increase performance.
fp16.note: Statement about the Apple GPU family, not a per-chip table. Source: WWDC20 session 10632 'Optimize Metal Performance for Apple silicon Macs' (2020), about the Apple shader core of Apple's GPUs; the session predates M2 to M6 and names no chip for the 16-bit ALU (it also says 'Apple GPUs are optimized for 16-bit data types.'). Read as: family-level, applies to every row only by that generality.

metal.quote: Metal 4 is compatible with M1 (and later) and A14 Bionic (and later) Apple chips.
metal.note: WWDC25 session 205 'Discover Metal 4' (2025): states support by 'M1 (and later)' and 'A14 Bionic (and later)'; a family-level statement, no per-chip list. Covers every M1 to M4 row by name; M5, M5 Pro/Max/Ultra and M6 only through 'and later'. The per-chip table is a PDF (blocked).
